title: Internal Strife, Lahore Unrest, and Sukha Singh’s Crossing

blocks.text: The page begins with disorder inside the Sikh world itself, where factional violence follows the killing of Kushal Singh and prompts retaliation against the Bhangis. Instead of a single united front, the narrative pauses to show how internal wounds can interrupt broader strategy.

It then returns to Lahore, where tensions flare into clashes with butchers and townspeople near the city gates. Urban hostility and factional confusion together create a turbulent setting in which bold action feels both risky and necessary.

Against that background Sukha Singh crosses the Ravi with a small chosen band and moves toward Abdali’s camp. His crossing is framed as the beginning of an audacious strike that will exchange safety for honor and direct confrontation.
